text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Tuesday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Turkey's President Suleyman Demireli, who began a two-day visit to Lithuania on Monday, declined at a press conference to comment on the political crisis back home.
- Lithuanian basketball star Rimas Kurtinaitis, 37, started his work as the head of the country's sport department.
- Belgium's Hydro Soil Service started reconstruction works in Klaipeda port.
- The average yield at Monday's auction for 28-day T-bills was a record low of 7.87 percent.

- If the elections were held tomorrow 15.7 percent of Lithuanians would vote for the rulling Homeland Union party, four percent less than a month before, Baltic Surveys most recent poll carried out in May said. The Centre Union would take 13 percent(+3) of votes, Democratic Labour party 9.6 (0) percent, Christian Democrtas 7.3 (+4)percent and Social Democrats 6.9 (+1) percent.
- Lithuania and Turkey signed a free trade agreement during the official visit of Turkish president Suleyman Demireli to Vilnius on Monday.
- The Vilnius prosecutor's office has started a case against former top officials of the Bank of Lithuania who are accused of lax banking supervision which led to banking crisis in December 1995.
- Lithuania's transport ministry approved the decision to merge the country's two airlines. Aviation company Lietuva will join Lithuanian Airlines as a daughter company.
